corrected_draft.description_long: Reuters reported that Trump made the announcement in a Truth Social post, saying he wanted to “clean house” and restore confidence in the justice system. corrected_draft.description_long: The January 29 order directed agency heads to report within 60 days on authorities or actions that might be used to combat antisemitism and to analyze pending administrative complaints involving higher-education institutions and alleged civil-rights violations related to campus antisemitism. The Attorney General’s report was also to inventory relevant court cases and identify actions taken or intended. The order encouraged use of civil-rights enforcement authorities and asked State, Education and Homeland Security to recommend ways for universities to identify and report certain noncitizen activity relevant to inadmissibility grounds. It did not itself create a general authorization to prosecute critics for material support of terrorism. A separate March 14 event involved federal agents searching two Columbia University dorm rooms under warrants while DOJ investigated possible terrorism-law violations connected to protests; Reuters reported that nobody was detained and no items were removed. Those dates and actions should remain separate.
